scope: Nine Wave32 bitwise operations in boolean_functions, including selected half and preservation of the other half. Per-bit AND/OR/XOR/NOT/XNOR truth tables are a direct specification-derived exact reference, independent of numeric rounding. Every truth-table input at each bit and selector is checked, with exhaustive half encodings and deterministic full words. Exact integer results are required even when the API semantics selector is loose.
diagnostics: Per-output assertion identifies operation, CPU, modifier and lane; no opaque golden digest is used.

scope: Six Wave32 add/sub/subrev/add3 operations. int64_t computes signed or unsigned widened sums/differences without overflow (three uint32_t inputs sum below 2^34); explicit clamp then uint32_t narrowing implements saturation or modulo 2^32. Independent literal boundaries check operand order, signed limits, borrow and ADD3 clamp behavior. This simple integer model is an exact oracle; fuzzy FP comparison is inapplicable.
diagnostics: Boundary/random tests trace operation, CPU, clamp and batch; literal cases separately expose saturation and operand-order regressions.

scope: The 20 scalar operations in scalar_integer_call, their immediate variants and additional sign-extension checks. Hardware digests cover result low/high words and SCC over 4096 boundary/random pairs, both incoming SCC values and both semantics. Immediate ADDK/MULK computed references use bounded int64_t arithmetic and explicit narrowing; literal ABS_DIFF cases preserve its wrap-before-absolute ordering. Aliasing checks are differential memory checks, not separate numerical oracles.
diagnostics: Each hardware failure identifies CPU, semantics, incoming SCC and one opcode/immediate row (4096 pairs). Literal boundaries and exhaustive immediate assertions complement those compact row digests; dense-domain checkpoints are not needed for these small rows.

scope: 84 RDNA4 Wave32 FP16/32/64 CMP/CMPX predicate entry points. Exact mask results are anchored by hardware captures across modifiers, masks and input-denormal policy. The independent integer-bit reference applies selectors, ABS then NEG, optional flush, NaN unordered handling and signed-zero equality; sign/magnitude order implements finite comparisons without host FP arithmetic. Every half encoding is checked with representative operand pairing, not all 2^32 half pairs. Optional exception-state behavior is reviewed separately.
diagnostics: Hardware digest identifies CPU, denormal policy, mask and predicate. Independent boundary/every-half tests report predicate/modifier/input batch. DPP capture and per-output routing checks complement each other.

scope: FP32 RCP/SQRT/RSQ/EXP/LOG exact implementations borrowed from rocjitsu, both architectures and wave widths. Dense domains use retained raw hardware digests; modifier/exponent/special-value domains have per-policy/per-modifier digests. Rocjitsu-generated cumulative checkpoints reproduce all five hardware totals. DPP comparisons to a non-DPP invocation check routing/alias behavior and do not independently prove the numeric model. Architecture-specific NaN and OMOD assertions remain literal anchors.
diagnostics: Dense captures now stop at the first failing 2^20-input interval. Modifier captures localize to operation, wave width, FP policy and modifier (8192 inputs).

scope: Bit scans count leading/trailing bits by an explicit loop; MBCNT counts selected bit positions below the physical destination lane and adds modulo 2^32. Literal all-zero/all-one sentinels and lane-number composition distinguish scan/count semantics. Wave64 DPP is independently hardware-anchored to physical destination lanes. Integer outputs require exact equality in either semantics.
diagnostics: Literal cases and per-output checks accompany the compact Wave64 DPP hardware digest. Pair/complement and population sweeps isolate individual bits; a failing digest need not be expanded into raw captures.

scope: Eight Wave32 extract/insert/mask/reverse/align/permute operations. The oracle reconstructs each destination bit from the source bit, explicit signed fill, reduced count or selector. All offset/width/source-bit combinations and all selector bytes are exercised. diagnostics: Computed checks identify individual output mismatches; literals identify boundary rules. PERM hardware hash is supplemented by EverySelectorAndSourceBit, so extra raw golden arrays are unnecessary.

scope: Seven Wave32 low/high 32-bit and signed/unsigned 24-bit products. Magnitudes multiply in uint64_t (maximum uint32_t product fits); signedness is restored with unsigned modulo arithmetic after any saturation. High-word extraction is explicit. Literal vectors cover signed minima, ignored upper bytes, high words and clamp. These are specification-derived integer references, not approximate numerical comparisons.

scope: Fourteen Wave32 signed/unsigned min/max/min3/max3/median and mixed min-max orderings. scope: Eight Wave32 shift/add/Boolean/packed-average combinations. scope: Four Wave32 signed/unsigned 16/24-bit multiply-add operations. Explicit half selection/sign extension and int64_t product plus 32-bit accumulator remain within int64_t range. scope: Twelve Wave32 single-half integer operations reuse the independently widened packed-half oracle only for the selected values. scope: Eight Wave32 half MAD/min3/max3/median signed/unsigned operations. scope: Twelve Wave32 packed integer operations. Each half is independently selected and computed in int64_t; saturation is applied only to the specified add/sub operations. scope: Six Wave32 32/64-bit shifts. The computed reference visits each output bit, selects the shifted source or explicit sign/zero fill, and reduces the count modulo width. This avoids undefined oversized/signed host shifts. Every count and source bit/complement, ignored count bits, masks and register-half aliases are exercised.
diagnostics: Per-word assertions show opcode, CPU and count; both register halves and untouched words are checked. No opaque digest.

scope: Four signed/unsigned packed 4-bit/8-bit dot products in both wave sizes. Base-radix decoding and int64_t accumulation are exact; clamp applies after the entire dot, avoiding x86 pairwise saturation. Rocjitsu ffc144c564c Dot4ClampPolicyMatchesArchitecture vectors explicitly anchor the hardware/manual discrepancy: DOT4 does saturate. Every element pair/position and modifier combinations supplement boundary/random tests in both semantics.
diagnostics: Per-output and literal rocjitsu policy vectors identify saturation/order regressions; no digest-only dependency.

scope: Nine Boolean and two conditional-selection Wave64 operations reuse the independent bitwise and selector models. Both semantics, selected halves, ignored CLAMP, DPP routes/all row masks, full/irregular EXEC and aliased destinations are compared per lane. The separate Wave32 strict-exact case covers all eleven entry points; floating-looking input words remain raw bits.
diagnostics: Failures print operation/modifier/lane/route, with guard checks; no numerical approximation or opaque digest.

scope: Six shift and eight bitfield Wave64 operations use the independent per-bit models, with full/irregular masks, lane-distinct inputs, all DPP row masks, aliasing and both semantics. DPP is rejected for 64-bit operands rather than silently routed. Upper-wave and multi-register outputs are checked explicitly.
diagnostics: Per-lane/per-word checks and guards complement the Wave32 literal witnesses. Bitfield failures report opcode/batch/lane; shifts compare each output word directly.

scope: Signed/unsigned 16/32/64-bit CMP/CMPX predicates in both wave sizes. Explicit sign-bit ordering plus unsigned magnitude comparisons avoids signed-conversion ambiguity, with half selectors handled before comparison. Hardware masks anchor predicate/modifier/EXEC behavior; boundary/random, DPP and Wave64 cases check exact scalar mask results. Chained CMPX proves inactive lanes cannot reactivate.
diagnostics: Hardware digests are per predicate/width/control row, supplemented by per-mask expected results and a focused chained-CMPX invariant.

scope: Wave32 16/32-bit conditional selection. The reference selects the condition-chosen source, then copies bits while applying only sign ABS/NEG and half selection/preservation. There is no floating arithmetic; exact bit comparison remains appropriate in loose mode. Hardware capture, every modifier/condition bit, independent EXEC, aliases and DPP test the nontrivial selector behavior.
diagnostics: Per-output computed comparisons and condition-bit tests complement per-variant hardware digests; no need for a larger raw golden corpus.

scope: FP16/32/64 CLASS/CMPX masks classify raw sign/exponent/fraction/quiet-bit fields, including both NaN classes, signed zero, denormals and infinities. An explicit ten-class Boolean model and known-class witnesses are hardware anchored. All class masks, every half encoding in Wave64, selectors, DPP and raw-class invariance under guest FP policies are tested. Output masks are exact even in loose semantics.
diagnostics: Per-variant hardware digests have per-mask/class/encoding companion assertions, avoiding dependence on a single broad digest.

scope: READLANE/WRITELANE/READFIRSTLANE in both wave sizes and semantics. Lane-tagged literal words make index modulo wave width and first-active selection directly observable; every wrapped index and active-lane pair is exercised. The zero-EXEC first-lane behavior is explicitly anchored. Scalar outputs may alias source storage, while other lanes and guards must remain unchanged.

scope: DS gather/scatter and force-inactive gather. Deterministic masks/offsets and exhaustive gather pairs exercise inactive-source and alias behavior; this is a simple routing oracle, not numerical reverse engineering.
diagnostics: Assertions identify architecture, direction, sample, alias and lane; focused address-overflow/collision and cross-half anchors provide additional localization.

scope: Both wave sizes, all 65536 offset encodings. scope: PERMLANE16/PERMLANEX16 scalar and per-lane selectors in both wave sizes. scope: Thirty scalar Boolean/shift/shift-add operations. Hardware result-low/result-high/SCC digests cover 4096 input pairs and both incoming SCC values, in both semantics and every CPU selector. scope: Forty-six scalar integer/floating/bit predicates. Hardware SCC digests cover 4096 inputs per opcode under eight FP states and both semantics. scope: DPP8 FMA/FMAC routing, FI, modifiers, masks and aliases. The captured corpus uses small integers. The computed corpus uses multiples of 1/8 in [-4,4]; products are multiples of 1/64 with magnitude at most 16, sums at most 20, and OMOD is a power-of-two scale. All nonzero results are exactly representable in binary32; explicit zero-sign/clamp handling anchors zeros. scope: DPP16 enumerates every accepted control encoding and covers FI/BOUND, row/bank enables, masks and aliases; invalid encodings are rejected. scope: Four signed/unsigned half extensions and saturating pair packs, both wave widths. scope: RDNA4 byte-to-FP32 and signed-nibble offsets in both widths. diagnostics: Byte/nibble DPP hardware digest now compares every output with the bounded exact reference and identifies CPU, EXEC, opcode, descriptor, modifier and lane.

scope: Five byte/nibble conversions, both architectures and widths, loose and strict exact semantics. The bounded dyadic encoding proof applies unchanged. The local OMOD policy table cites RDNA3 ISA 7.2.3.1. Every selected input, all eight guest policies and output modifier combinations are checked with deterministic unselected-bit noise. DPP adds mixed EXEC, aliases and guards. Invalid modes preserve output. These exactly representable results need no fuzzy tolerance.

scope: Signed-half-to-byte saturation and RDNA4 FP16 field packing in both widths. Saturation uses direct integer limits. FP packing selects halves, quiets NaNs and applies ABS then NEG without arithmetic. The 66 gfx1201 digests anchor every half encoding across modifiers, including NaN handling. Wave32 and strict-exact Wave64 now check the captured inputs individually against the field reference as well as retaining the hardware digest. DPP/mask/alias tests compose these operations with routing. Exact optional-state reporting remains explicitly unsupported; loose state preservation is tested. No general numerical rounding equivalence is inferred.
diagnostics: Encoding captures now identify variant, CPU and exact input index in both widths. DPP hardware digest has computed routing/alias companions; literal saturation cases distinguish clamp and preserved-half behavior.

scope: Four FP8/BF8 widening operations, both wave widths. Finite codes have at most four significant bits and exponent ranges entirely representable in binary32, so direct integer re-encoding is exact. Raw gfx1201 hardware digests cover every code without NaN canonicalization and anchor exceptional encodings including NaN sign. The capture test now checks the computed decoder per code alongside the retained hardware total. Every packed pair, byte/half selection, unselected-bit perturbation, masks, destination overlap and guards are checked. DPP is tested for single-result forms and explicitly rejected for two-result forms. Wave64 regroups the Wave32 numerical capture; it is not a native Wave64 hardware capture. Exact assertions are appropriate even in loose semantics for this lossless widening.
diagnostics: Raw capture failures identify opcode, CPU, width, output register and code. Independent literal boundaries and per-output selector/routing checks complement the NaN-canonicalized DPP digest.

scope: Four packed/stochastic FP32-to-FP8/BF8 operations in both widths. Stored gfx1201 outputs anchor special values, overflow saturation, sign modifiers, destination placement and stochastic seed alignment; strict exact calls use these goldens directly. Both capture tests now also validate the computed reference directly against those outputs, independently of GoC. The reference quantizes in output-spacing units using double arithmetic, explicit nearest-even rounding or truncated seed addition. Deterministic boundary/adjacent/random inputs, six seed patterns and alias/DPP corpora provide supplemental model checks; agreement there is not a proof of arbitrary-input hardware equivalence. Retain the goldens for the empirical seed/special-value rules. Exact encoded comparisons also test destination-byte preservation; no blanket fuzzy replacement is justified for these structural checks.
diagnostics: Captured tests report source, seed, column and CPU in both widths. Boundary checks report source and second operand; the DPP digest has computed per-output routing companions. Captured-domain equivalence is explicit, not inferred solely from agreement with GoC.

scope: Six normalized signed/unsigned integer conversions from FP32/FP16, both widths. These are loose/fallback implementations: strict exact is explicitly rejected. The independent model multiplies the integer significand by 32767 or 65535 (less than 2^40), then performs one ties-even integer shift, avoiding a host FP product rounding into a false midpoint. Captured outputs anchor saturation, NaNs, ties and ignored modifiers. Tests now validate that model directly against all stored capture columns, without using GoC as the oracle. Every half encoding, every integer rounding boundary and adjacent float, deterministic full words, modifiers, masks and aliases are covered. Exact comparison of resulting integer fields is intentional; fuzzy FP tolerance would not test their rounding or preserved destination halves. Captured agreement is not a universal bit-exact API claim.
diagnostics: Per-lane computed checks report operands and mode. Both literal hardware corpora now report source, column and CPU, including Wave64. DPP final digest has companion per-output routing tests.

scope: Three RDNA4 packed FP32-to-FP16-RTZ or signed/unsigned integer conversions, both widths, loose/fallback only. Integer outputs use explicit truncation and saturation. The FP16 reference binary-searches for the greatest finite half magnitude no larger than the input; sign restoration implements RTZ. Literal captures anchor NaN fields, infinity, saturation and ignored output modifiers, and now directly validate the computed reference as well as GoC. Every half boundary and neighboring FP32 word, exponent/sign boundaries, deterministic full words, flags, DPP, aliases and guards are tested. Exact encoded comparisons deliberately check the specified quantization and packing; this is stronger regression evidence for the current loose path, not an assertion of supported strict exact semantics.
diagnostics: Computed checks identify operation, flags, operands and lane. Hardware corpora identify source, column, CPU and saturation in both widths. NaN-canonicalized DPP hash is supplemented by raw literal captures and per-output reference checks.

scope: Nine packed/normalized conversion operations across RDNA3/RDNA4 and Wave32/64. This integration suite reuses the independently computed quantization references reviewed in the numerical family tests. It exercises all guest policies and modifiers, ordinary plus two representative DPP routes, mixed EXEC, three destination/source alias placements and guards across CPU paths. It does not claim native hardware captures for every architecture or policy. Strict exact is rejected, optional exact global-state reporting is rejected for applicable operations, and loose reporting leaves state unchanged. Numerical result checks are exact quantization/field checks, not arbitrary approximate arithmetic.
diagnostics: Whole-buffer assertions report architecture, width, opcode, policy, modifier, route, alias and CPU. Individual numerical failures can be localized using the companion family tests; no large digest is the sole oracle.

scope: RDNA4 FP32-to-byte packing and signed-nibble-to-FP32 offset. The byte reference explicitly applies ABS/NEG, classifies NaNs/sign, clamps to 0..255 and rounds significand bits ties-even before replacing only the selected byte of C. Every half-integer boundary and adjacent float is exercised for all byte positions and modifiers, with deterministic full-word alias/guard/mask checks. Literal hardware captures now validate the computed reference independently of GoC. Byte conversion is loose/fallback-only; the separate architecture tests explicitly reject strict exact. The nibble reference is exact bounded dyadic encoding and all selected nibbles/unselected bits are checked. Integer quantization and byte preservation intentionally use exact comparisons rather than fuzzy floating comparison.
diagnostics: Hardware capture failures identify row/column/CPU. The retained DPP hardware digest now checks each result against the computed routing/quantization reference with CPU, EXEC, descriptor, modifier and lane context.

scope: FP16 field packing and FP32 byte packing across both architectures and wave widths. Reuses the separately hardware-anchored field and quantization references. All guest policies, modifiers, full/zero/mixed masks and four destination placements are exercised; DPP tests cover the routing descriptors with representative modifiers. Strict exact FP16 packing is accepted only for RDNA4, with a literal sNaN-quieting result; strict exact byte packing is rejected. Optional exact state returns unsupported without touching output, and loose calls preserve optional state. This integration coverage is not a native hardware capture for every architecture/policy combination.
diagnostics: DPP comparisons now trace opcode, architecture, width, CPU, guest policy and descriptor. Other whole-buffer checks have configuration context; literal exact-support assertions separately anchor the accepted behavior.

scope: Six integer/FP32 conversion operations in both widths, loose/fallback semantics. The independent integer-only reference derives nearest-even integer-to-FP32 rounding from discarded bits, and truncating/nearest/floor FP32-to-integer results from exact significand fractions with saturation. Literal witnesses distinguish positive-tie nearest rounding, negative floor, NaN policy and signed limits. Exponent/precision boundaries, deterministic full words and all modifiers are covered. Hardware ordinary/DPP digests already compare individual outputs to the model. Masks, aliases, guards, Wave64 high lanes and optional-state preservation/rejection have dedicated checks. Exact comparisons intentionally test conversion rounding and integer results; this does not imply supported strict exact semantics, which validation rejects.
diagnostics: Hardware assertions now include CPU, EXEC, opcode, DPP descriptor, modifier variant and lane. Computed helpers already print input/result/mode and literal witnesses independently anchor rounding rules.

scope: Six conversions across RDNA3/RDNA4 and both widths. Numerical integration reuses the independent integer reference. A literal conversion of integer 3 anchors architecture-dependent OMOD gating, citing rocjitsu effective_omod: RDNA3 requires output flush and IEEE=0, RDNA4 does not. All eight guest policies, all operation modifiers, ordinary plus seven DPP routes, mixed EXEC and source/destination overlap are exercised with boundary inputs and deterministic word patterns. Strict exact is explicitly rejected; applicable exact optional-state requests reject without changing state or destination. These are loose-path tests rather than hardware captures for every architecture/policy combination.
diagnostics: Whole-buffer comparisons identify architecture, width, opcode, guest mode, modifier, route, alias and CPU. Literal scaling witnesses distinguish policy errors from numerical reference errors.

scope: Six int32/FP32/FP64 conversions in both widths, loose/fallback only. The reference decodes integer significands and re-encodes with an explicit ties-even shift and separate normal/subnormal ranges; integer outputs truncate and saturate without host FP casts. Literal cases independently anchor overflow, signed zero, rounding ties, subnormals and conversion-before-OMOD ordering. Narrowing midpoint tests span every FP32 exponent with six representative fractions and adjacent FP64 encodings, not every possible midpoint. Full-word random draws are explicitly sequenced. Exact finite checks test quantization; quiet NaNs are compared by class without fixing payload/sign. Alias tests cover split words, overlapping destinations, masks and guards; their finite-only Wave64 inputs avoid incorrectly requiring NaN payload agreement. Strict exact is explicitly rejected, and DPP is invalid for these forms.
diagnostics: Per-lane numeric helper reports operation, flags, mode, input, expected and actual. Literal cases anchor model independence. There is no opaque hardware digest requiring checkpoints; fixtures are literal numerical witnesses, not claimed hardware captures.

scope: Six conversions across both architectures and widths. Literal conversion/scaling of 3 anchors RDNA3 OMOD gating (RDNA3 ISA 7.2.3.1 and rocjitsu effective_omod). Boundary inputs, all modifiers and guest policies, mixed EXEC, swapped source/destination halves and overlapping output registers use the integer reference. A separate NaN suite exercises both signs and signaling/quiet payloads, requiring quiet NaN class for floating results and zero for integer results, rather than payload equality. Strict exact and applicable exact optional-state requests are rejected without destination/state changes. This is loose-path integration evidence, not native hardware equivalence for all modes.
diagnostics: Whole-buffer assertions report architecture, width, opcode, policy, modifier, alias and CPU. NaN assertions have configuration context and finite alias tests remain independent of payload policy.

scope: Six integer/FP16/FP32 conversion operations, both widths, loose/fallback only. Independent integer-significand re-encoding supplies nearest-even narrowing and exact widening; float-to-integer decodes and saturates directly. Hardware literals anchor overflow saturation, OMOD order and subnormal thresholds. Every half encoding is swept for two modifier endpoints and both overflow settings; every positive/negative finite-half narrowing midpoint and adjacent FP32 word is covered across OMOD settings. Deterministic full-word tests cover all modifiers, with source/destination half selection, masks, aliases and guards. Quiet NaN comparison permits payload/sign differences but requires unchanged unselected destination bits. Captures remain the evidence for empirical edge rules; model agreement outside them is not universal hardware proof. Strict exact rejection is explicit.
diagnostics: Literal captures identify source, column, CPU and overflow mode in both widths. DPP hardware total retains companion per-output checks, now with CPU, overflow, EXEC, opcode, descriptor, variant, lane and numeric result context.

scope: Six conversions across both architectures and widths. All sixteen guest policy/overflow combinations, modifiers, ordinary/seven DPP routes and aliases use the independently computed conversion model with architecture policy adjustments. The literal integer-3 witness anchors OMOD gating. Every-half widening separately checks raw sign/payload/signaling bits following rocjitsu cvt_f32_f16: RDNA3 IEEE=0 with no arithmetic output modifier preserves signaling bits, whereas RDNA4 or IEEE mode quiets them; input-flush maps half subnormals to signed zero. This raw check is intentionally stricter than the general loose quiet-NaN comparator. API calls remain loose and strict exact is rejected; upstream-derived reference behavior does not imply supported strict semantics.
diagnostics: Architecture assertions identify width, opcode, policy, modifier, route, alias, CPU and lane with actual/expected values. Exhaustive widening failures identify the precise half encoding. No opaque digest requires additional fixtures.

scope: TRUNC/CEIL/RNDNE/FLOOR FP32 across both architectures and widths. Hardware result digests cover 8192 inputs per policy/modifier with canonicalized NaNs; CPU selectors rotate by batch, not a full CPU-by-input Cartesian product. Computed DPP reference uses double trunc/ceil/floor and explicit ties-even rounding; binary32 inputs and resulting integral values are exactly representable except intentional output scaling overflow. Strict exact DPP/alias tests are differential against an un-routed call, so they prove routing/control invariance rather than independent numerical correctness. Literal raw NaN outputs inherited from rocjitsu establish unconditional quieting and preserved payload/sign. Exact optional state is not requested by this integration test; removal of a vacuous unchanged-local assertion makes that limit explicit.
diagnostics: Hardware digests localize to operation, architecture, width, policy and modifier (8192 inputs), with computed DPP and literal NaN companions. Exact DPP failures now include routing, guest mode and host settings.

scope: Loose/fallback FP32 FRAC uses two retained 8192-input gfx1201 result corpora across policies/modifiers and both architectures/widths, with CPU selectors rotating by batch. It compares canonicalized hardware result hashes; this is retained empirical regression evidence, not a supported strict-exact path. Literal FP32/FP16 cases independently anchor zero signs, tiny negative inputs staying below one, integer boundaries, source/destination half selection, guest flushing and in-place mixed EXEC. Strict exact and exact reporting are rejected before writes; loose optional state is unchanged. The hash test uses only captured result hashes, not the stored raw result/exception pair hashes, and does not claim exception generation. General approximate unary calibration is reviewed separately.
diagnostics: Small literal boundary cases complement per-policy/modifier hardware hashes. The two corpora distinguish broad random/exponent coverage; each digest failure currently localizes to 8192 inputs, not an individual input. No new reverse-engineered exact model or expanded golden array is introduced.

scope: FP32/FP64 exponent extraction, both architectures and widths. The reference finds the leading significand bit and combines it with the exponent field, mapping zero/nonfinite to zero without host floating arithmetic. Every exponent field with four representative tails, every subnormal leading position and deterministic mt19937_64 words are tested. Exact equality is appropriate for integer results in both semantics. FP32 strict-exact hardware digests now include independent per-input checks with guest input flushing. FP64 remains loose/fallback and explicitly rejects strict exact and DPP. Modifier/mask/alias tests include split-source words, guards and optional-state rejection/preservation. Exact optional state is not requested in the DPP numerical tests; state assertions now apply only to loose calls that pass its address.
diagnostics: FP32 hardware failure now identifies semantics, architecture, width, flags, modifier and precise corpus input. Literal and computed boundary checks supplement retained hashes; FP64 architecture checks identify policy and modifier.

scope: FP32 mantissa extraction across both architectures and widths, loose and strict exact. Retained hardware result hashes cover 8192 inputs for guest policies and modifiers, canonicalizing NaNs; CPU selector rotates by batch. Literal exact special-value tests separately check signed zero, infinity and quieted NaN payload/sign under source modifiers. Every subnormal leading-bit position has literal mantissa 0.5 or signed zero when flushed. DPP expected values come from an un-routed exact call, making them routing/alias/control checks rather than independent numerical evidence. Optional exact reporting is explicitly unsupported; loose state preservation is checked only when the pointer is passed. Stored raw result/exception pair hashes are not used to claim reporting support.
diagnostics: Per-policy/modifier hardware hashes have literal special/subnormal companions. DPP compares lanes individually. Removed misleading exact-state expectation for null-pointer calls; numerical hardware evidence remains unchanged.

scope: FP32/FP64 LDEXP in both widths, loose/fallback only. The reference scales in long double with extreme exponents clamped after they already force destination overflow/underflow, then rounds to destination precision before OMOD. Power-of-two scaling introduces no significand multiplication error within the wider range; the current x86 long-double range covers FP64 boundaries. This portability assumption is not a claim for platforms where long double equals double. Literal subnormal ties, signed zeros and overflow supplement exponent-field/target-boundary sweeps and random pairs. Exact finite comparisons intentionally check scaling/rounding; NaNs use class checks. DPP applies only to FP32; split-word aliases and masked stores have separate coverage. Strict exact/reporting errors are explicit. The random input/exponent pair now has sequenced draws; the former emplace_back argument order was toolchain-dependent.
diagnostics: Computed checks use per-batch traces and literal boundaries; DPP hardware digest has independent reference companions. No new golden data is required.

scope: Both LDEXP formats, architectures and widths. Long-double power-of-two reference is combined with explicit guest input/output flushing and RDNA3 OMOD gating. Literal witnesses distinguish flushing from scaling. All guest policies/modifiers and representative alias layouts cover mixed EXEC; FP32 DPP uses every routing descriptor with a representative modifier. NaNs are checked by class or clamp-to-zero, not payload agreement. Strict exact and exact optional-state reporting reject without writes. These loose numerical checks do not assert universal hardware bit-exactness.
diagnostics: Literal policy witnesses and configuration-tagged whole-buffer checks supplement per-lane DPP and NaN tests. No large digest is the sole oracle.

scope: FP16 LDEXP and exponent extraction in both widths, loose/fallback only. Half decode is exact in double; power-of-two scaling retains significand bits until explicitly rounded to FP16, with large finite overflow represented by a finite sentinel for saturation provenance. FREXP reference uses the defined exponent of the exactly decoded half. Every half encoding is tested at boundary exponents; every signed 16-bit exponent uses sixteen representative inputs, not their full Cartesian product. Hardware digest covers every half with five exponents, four OMOD values and both overflow settings, anchoring empirical stage-order rules. Literal ties/overflow and modifier/mask/alias/DPP checks complement it. Preserved halves use exact comparison and NaNs use class checks. Strict exact and reporting are rejected.
diagnostics: Large hardware total has per-output computed sweeps and literal rounding witnesses. Those companion tests identify opcode, CPU, overflow, mode, exponent and input block, so the total is not the sole diagnostic.

scope: FP16 scaling/exponent extraction across both architectures and widths. Reuses the independently decoded half reference with explicit guest flush/OMOD/overflow rules. All guest settings and modifiers are checked with boundary values, aliases, guards and mixed EXEC; routing cycles across modifiers rather than forming a full Cartesian product. Every half encoding additionally runs in Wave64 under eight guest policies with a selected modifier and varying exponent. NaN class checks preserve the unselected half. Strict exact and optional exact state reject, loose state remains unchanged. The integration model is not native hardware evidence for every mode.
diagnostics: Literal policies distinguish input/output flush and architecture scaling gates. Per-output assertions identify architecture, width, opcode, policy, modifier, alias, CPU and lane; exhaustive sweep identifies half encoding.

scope: Raw 16/32-bit moves, both widths. Direct field selection, sign-bit ABS/NEG and preservation of unselected halves give exact references without floating arithmetic. Hardware digest anchors ignored OMOD/CLAMP, including signaling NaNs and subnormals; it now has per-lane computed companions. Every half encoding/sign modifier is covered, and DPP tests use before-images to catch in-place ordering errors. Wave64 tests cover row masks, FI/bound controls, upper lanes and DPP8. Raw equality is required in loose semantics too.
diagnostics: Hardware capture now identifies width, modifier, half selection and lane; CPU is scoped. Exhaustive half and per-lane DPP checks supplement the retained digest.

scope: Four relative-register move forms, both widths, plus ordinary MOV sign-modifier composition. Explicit widened register indices model bounds, source fallback to register zero, invalid destination discard, packed M0 offsets and the 255 offset limit independent of allocated storage. Before-images and direct bitwise ABS/NEG after routing provide exact references; integer/raw comparisons are appropriate in either semantics. Tests cover empty files, overflowed base indices, guards, aliases and inactive/upper lanes. These tests select baseline CPU; CPU-level raw MOV routing is covered in move_test.cpp rather than claimed here.
diagnostics: Whole-file comparisons identify opcode, M0 and route; literal offset-limit cases expose bounds errors, and per-word sign-modifier checks identify width/opcode/modifier/route/word.

scope: Raw 16/32-bit swaps, relative swaps and PERMLANE64 in both widths. Independent before-image exchange and lane XOR32 mapping are exact field/routing references. Half tests preserve untouched bits even when exchanging halves of one register. Invalid relative operand cancels both writes, tested separately from allocation-size limits with offsets 255/256/299 and widened addressing. Native Wave32/Wave64 gfx1201 digests anchor relative-swap semantics. Wave32 PERMLANE64 is a no-op with no EXEC parameter. Masks include zero/full/alternating/single upper lanes; all available CPU selectors are exercised.
diagnostics: Native hardware digests identify width/opcode/mask and have literal bounds and per-output swap companions. Direct field-copy models suffice; fuzzy comparisons would weaken raw-bit behavior.

scope: Scalar hardware-register access and mode updates for RDNA3/RDNA4. Independent per-bit insertion/extraction checks all register IDs and offset/width combinations against manual-defined writable fields, with privilege, reserved-bit preservation, clock halves and literal architecture differences. Retained gfx1201 MODE/EXCP_FLAG_USER capture digests anchor the per-bit model on captured inputs; this is not arbitrary numerical reverse engineering. Tests cover optional snapshots, null outputs, unavailable exact state, error precedence and unchanged outputs, plus host-control preservation while modifying guest MODE. Mode instructions run every available CPU selector; scalar register enumeration uses baseline. Exact raw register comparisons apply in loose semantics too.
diagnostics: Hardware read/write corpora now report register, seed, source pattern and field boundaries, and check each output independently before the retained group digest. Literal and exhaustive field tests supplement capture evidence.

scope: Constant true/false integer and floating CMP/CMPX predicates in both wave widths, all available CPU selectors and both semantics. Boolean constants filtered by EXEC and independently modeled DPP destination enablement give directly justified exact masks; no approximate floating arithmetic is involved. Null source operands demonstrate that inputs are not read. Tests cover upper lanes, empty EXEC, ignored supported modifiers, invalid flags with preserved results and unsupported 64-bit DPP. Floating exact optional state is explicitly unsupported (including precedence over empty EXEC and bad flags); loose requested state is preserved. These tests do not claim floating exception generation.
diagnostics: Per-mask assertions and DPP configuration diagnostics; explicit sentinel values expose partial writes on errors. No golden array or fuzzy comparison is needed for constant predicate masks.

scope: Six add/subtract/reverse-subtract operations with and without carry-in, both widths and both semantics. Unsigned 64-bit arithmetic independently derives 32-bit results, borrow/carry and saturation. Direct captured values and masks now validate this reference without depending on GoC; the DPP capture retains its hardware digest plus per-lane routed arithmetic checks. Deterministic mt19937 boundary/random streams, chained 64-bit word arithmetic, all CPU selectors, inactive-lane carry clearing, scalar/vector aliases, guards and zero-EXEC/error preservation are covered. Wave64 scalar alias reference is differential, supplemented by independent boundary and chained-word tests.
diagnostics: Hardware output checks identify operation/CPU/clamp/EXEC/lane; DPP digest companions additionally identify source carry, route, host rounding and semantics. Existing masked-alias tests retain complete before-image comparisons.

scope: Four RDNA3/RDNA4 signed/unsigned wide MAD spellings in Wave32. The extended-sum model computes product plus accumulator, extracts bit 64 before saturation, and distinguishes the signed extended sign from overflow. It shares the production Uint128 utility, so arithmetic-helper independence is limited; gfx1201 Cartesian digests and literal signed overflow/sign witnesses remain independent anchors. Captured outputs now have per-input model companions. Deterministic mt19937 streams, all CPU selectors, overlapping destination registers and scalar output, EXEC, saturation, host settings and validation are covered. Loose mask/alias tests use unclamped operations; clamped coverage here is exact, supplemented by both-semantics Wave64 tests.
diagnostics: Retained digest identifies operation/CPU/clamp/EXEC; new per-input and scalar-mask checks locate Cartesian failures. Literal positive/negative overflow cases explain scalar output semantics.

scope: Four narrow-factor and four wide-result Wave64 MAD entry points. Bounded 64-bit arithmetic handles signed/unsigned 16/24-bit factors and explicit extension/clamp. Wide reference inherits the Wave32 captured/literal validation and shared-Uint128 limitation. Both semantics/all CPU selectors, all narrow half/clamp modes, DPP row masks, upper-lane EXEC, source/destination aliases and guards are exercised. Wide overlapping D0/D1 and scalar output straddling lanes31/32 tests use each single-bit mask and its complement. Scalar alias integration includes differential checks; independent wide-result checks remain separate. Unsupported DPP and empty-EXEC behavior are tested.
diagnostics: Per-lane narrow and overlapping-wide checks identify operation/batch or mask bit. Wide arithmetic/guard assertions supplement the Wave32 hardware digests; no separate native Wave64 hardware capture is claimed.

scope: Thirty-five Wave64 add/subtract/multiply/select/ternary entry points. References use bounded widened arithmetic, magnitude multiplication with explicit sign restoration, scalar comparisons and sorting; these directly implement integer ISA rules, so exact comparison remains appropriate in loose semantics. Boundary Cartesian inputs and deterministic unsigned mixing cover both semantics/all CPU selectors, supported saturation, reverse-source DPP, all row masks, upper/inactive lanes, whole-register aliases and guard preservation. No numerical hardware-equivalence claim is inferred from SIMD/scalar agreement. Zero EXEC and unsupported flags/routes are separately checked.
diagnostics: Direct per-lane assertions identify opcode, batch, lane and mode; guard checks expose writes outside the wave. Shared test references are separately reviewed in their Wave32 families.

scope: Thirty-four selected-half and packed Wave64 integer entry points, including signed/unsigned MAD. Widened bounded arithmetic, explicit signed extension, scalar sorting, masked shifts and half insertion provide simple ISA-derived exact references. Both semantics/all CPU selectors cover every encoded half-selector/clamp combination, DPP where supported, row masks, upper/inactive lanes, aliases and destination guards. Input patterns combine integer boundaries and defined unsigned mixing; mode-dependent generation is deterministic but not an exhaustive Cartesian input/mode product. Packed DPP rejection and pre-access validation/zero EXEC are explicit.
diagnostics: Per-lane comparisons include opcode/mode/lane/route; raw-word comparison verifies untouched halves. No fuzzy numerical comparison is applicable.

scope: Eight Wave32 SAD/MSAD/QSAD/MQSAD variants. Independent radix decomposition, signed widened absolute differences and widened accumulators model byte/halfword/word windows, zero-byte masking, independent packed saturation and wrapping. Directly justified integer rules are complemented by literal overflow/window outputs and retained RX9070 DPP digest. Full byte-pair and halfword sweeps, deterministic mt19937 streams, every byte-zero pattern and unused high source byte, all CPU selectors, EXEC, coincident destination/source aliases, DPP and guards are covered. Main exhaustive loops use loose semantics; compact literal witnesses now exercise both semantics with STRICT. Exact host-state integration is separate.
diagnostics: Per-register/lane reference failures include opcode/flags/clamp. Hardware DPP now adds per-output checks with opcode/CPU/EXEC/route/clamp/lane while preserving the independent final digest.

scope: Eight Wave64 SAD variants, both semantics with STRICT and every available CPU selector. Independent widened byte/window reference is shared with Wave32; no new native Wave64 capture is claimed. Defined mt19937 draws include near-overflow accumulators and zero-byte masking. Supported DPP row controls, high EXEC bits, source aliases, all-register guards, empty EXEC and unsupported routes are tested. Compact hand-computed quad-window differences independently test below/at/above each accumulator limit and coincident destinations, including masks selecting lanes31/32.
diagnostics: Per-lane/per-result checks identify opcode and alias; literal threshold cases also report CPU/clamp/coincident layout. Threshold references do not call the general SAD oracle.

scope: Signed/unsigned packed Wave32 integer MAD. Explicit half extraction/sign extension and int64 product-plus-addend are bounded (unsigned maximum below 2^32); clamp precedes 16-bit narrowing. All 128 half-selection/clamp combinations, boundary triples, each source encoding with deterministic other operands, all CPU selectors and all 15 whole-register alias partitions are tested. Primary sweeps use loose semantics; literal full-precision overflow and cross-half witnesses now run both semantics with STRICT. Wave64 packed variants have separate both-semantics coverage in integer16_wave64_test.cpp. Invalid negation flags preserve results, empty EXEC and host-state behavior are checked.
diagnostics: Mode sweeps carry sign/CPU/mode context and alias failures report EXEC. Small literal witnesses independently anchor clamp-before-narrowing and half selection; no hardware capture is claimed.

scope: RDNA3 and RDNA4 nonconstant FP16/32/64 CMP/CMPX predicates, both wave widths. Bitwise sign/magnitude ordering with explicit NaN, signed-zero, input-flush and half-selection rules supplies exact predicate masks; RDNA4 predicate hardware evidence is in the separately reviewed float_compare family. Both semantics, every CPU selector, eight guest policies and all ABS/NEG/half modifiers are covered on boundary and deterministic mixed inputs. RDNA3 DPP includes aliased scalar results in upper source words. RDNA3 requested exact state is explicitly unsupported with atomic failure; RDNA4 reporting is separately covered in compare_exceptions. State preservation is asserted only when the test actually passes its pointer. Host-control checks do not serve as result or state-generation oracles.
diagnostics: Opcode-scoped policy comparisons and independent raw predicates; existing optional-state error tests preserve scalar result and state including empty EXEC. No native RDNA3 hardware capture is claimed.

scope: Eighty-four RDNA4 Wave64 predicate APIs. Independent raw ordering reference covers strict exact modifiers, input flushing, DPP row controls, upper-lane EXEC and predicate output aliasing into source words33/34. Captured per-pair exception data is reused at lanes0/31/32/63, including empty EXEC and signaling CLAMP; the captured classifications are not claimed to be a separate native Wave64 capture. Predicate routing loops select all CPUs; exact exception-pair loops select baseline and loose opt-out checks select the highest available CPU. Architecture integration separately covers loose results. Invalid-call preservation and zero-EXEC state behavior are explicit.
diagnostics: Per-pair exception failures now identify predicate, pair, signaling, flush and EXEC. Per-mask predicate checks identify modifier and route; hardware fixture stores individual exception results rather than an opaque digest.

scope: Twenty-eight scalar and eighty-four RDNA4 Wave32 vector predicates. gfx1201 captured 12x12 operand pairs anchor invalid/input-denormal flags across denormal and signaling modes, with OR accumulation and inactive-lane suppression. Reporting/nonreporting predicate results now both check the independent bitwise ordering model rather than only one another. Scalar literal ISA truth-table rows separately anchor less/equal/greater/unordered, signed zero, NaN and ignored upper-half inputs. DPP reduction uses captured per-pair flags after routing/half selection and tests result/source aliasing. All CPU selectors, loose skipping, optional output, invalid-call preservation and host-state checks are covered. RDNA3 exact reporting remains explicitly unsupported in architecture tests.
diagnostics: Hardware pair checks now report opcode/CPU/pair/denormal/signaling/EXEC and independently verify predicates. Literal scalar references avoid relying on the same order transform; captured flags remain independent numerical evidence.

scope: Nine RDNA4 FP32 ternary selections plus five RDNA3 spellings in Wave32/Wave64. Integer ordering/sorting and explicit nested selection provide computed loose references; literal cases anchor zero ties, NaN precedence and RDNA3 IEEE behavior. Raw equality intentionally checks selection and binary power-of-two OMOD with explicit flush/overflow/clamp boundaries rather than approximate accumulated arithmetic. Deterministic mt19937 patterns, all 512 modifiers, guest policies, CPU selectors, DPP, EXEC and aliases/guards are covered. Route/mode pairing in integration loops is stratified, not full Cartesian coverage. Strict exact is rejected; exact optional reporting is unsupported, loose requested state is unchanged. Reference shares production bit-cast helpers only; no arbitrary hardware equivalence is claimed.
diagnostics: Literal triple tests report operands and operation; broad integration checks report opcode/guest/width/mode/CPU/register/lane. No new golden fixture is needed for loose selection references.

scope: Legacy Wave32 binary FP16/32/64 and packed FP16 plus ten half/single ternary entry points. Finite literal operands and direct masks/half preservation establish ordinary results and aliases for every available CPU selector. Ternary references select exactly representable small integers, with explicit lossless half encoding. Literal binary cases cover signed zeros, NaN-versus-number, infinities and denormals. These are loose-only spelling tests; strict exact and requested exact state must fail without writes. Broader architecture, modifier and special-value behavior is covered in minmax/half_minmax and binary families.
diagnostics: Compact literals and opcode/CPU/mask/alias diagnostics; no fuzzy comparison is needed for selected exact operands. Error tests preserve destination and state sentinels.

scope: Nine RDNA4 half ternary selections and five RDNA3 spellings, both wave widths. Sortable integer keys, nested selection and independently decoded double/half rounding model provide loose references. All half encodings for one input with deterministic other operands, boundary triples, 8192 modifiers, overflow selection, CPU selectors, masks, aliases and untouched halves are exercised. Literal architecture cases separately enforce payload/zero ordering, including every legacy A encoding selected against quiet NaNs. Two retained median hardware digests anchor signed zeros and canonicalized NaNs; per-input companions now localize failures. Guest-policy integration uses stratified selector/routes. Strict exact and exact global state remain unsupported; loose state is preserved.
diagnostics: Hardware median tests now report CPU/input index before retained totals; NaN digest still canonicalizes sign/payload exactly as before. General half comparisons allow NaN classification while explicit architecture witnesses check payloads; finite selections/scaling and preserved bits use raw equality.

scope: Wave32 DPP integration for nine half ternary selections, loose-only. Two gfx1201 digests cover finite inputs and OMOD boundaries with per-lane reference checks. Defined uint32 LCG draws, reduced deliberate EXEC set for nondefault modes, whole-register alias layouts, guards and preserved halves are covered; separate loops exercise every 8192 modifier combination with all seven DPP descriptors and both overflow settings on all CPU selectors. Integer selection followed by power-of-two scaling and explicit half quantization justifies raw finite result checks; random NaNs are canonicalized. Invalid DPP and strict-exact rejection are explicit. This family does not implement or establish exact numerical semantics.
diagnostics: Hardware failures identify CPU/opcode/modifier/EXEC/lane; broad random tests have configuration traces and retained independent hardware hashes. Reduced mask cross-product is the previously measured audit optimization.

scope: Four cube operations on both architectures and wave widths. Production follows borrowed rocjitsu shared/cube.h; numeric reference independently uses ordered FP comparisons and double power-of-two scaling with explicit flush/overflow. Reference now checks retained literal gfx1201 outputs directly, and both-width Cartesian corpora compare each input before the captured hash. Captures establish equivalence on their domain, not exhaustive arbitrary-input proof. Raw exact comparisons are justified by axis selection/sign changes and exactly representable normal binary scaling with explicit endpoints; NaN/payload behavior remains hardware/upstream anchored. All CPU selectors, 512 modifiers, deterministic mt19937 bits, tie ordering, EXEC, aliases, guards, DPP and host settings are exercised. RDNA3 IEEE/DX10/OMOD differences have upstream-derived literal witnesses in both semantics.
diagnostics: Cartesian failures identify CPU/column/input, retaining hardware hashes. DPP digest has all-modifier routed-reference and literal companions rather than newly duplicating its large loop. Wave64 reuses the same per-output corpus; no new native Wave64 capture is claimed.

scope: FP32/64 DIV_FIXUP policy integration, RDNA3/RDNA4 and Wave32/Wave64. Independent long-double decode/classification selects raw quotient or special-case outputs and exactly rescales normal significands; it relies on the wider long-double range of the validated x86 builds. Borrowed division-test literals establish preservation of the tiny provisional quotient while flushing denominator/numerator only. Deterministic sequenced mt19937 pairs, all CPU selectors, all modifiers, eight guest policies, masks and cross-register aliases are covered. Semantics is stratified by mode parity rather than fully crossed. RDNA3 exact state rejection is tested atomically; successful reporting evidence belongs to div_fixup_test.cpp, not this review. State preservation checks now apply only to loose calls actually passing the pointer.
diagnostics: Full register comparisons identify architecture/width/type/guest/mode/CPU. Independent raw special-case witnesses and unsupported-state checks supplement computed references. These are exact selection/scaling comparisons, not fuzzy general division estimates.

scope: FP32/64 DIV_FMAS on both architectures and widths. Broad random policy/alias test is explicitly differential: RDNA4 exact GoC output with effective OMOD becomes expected output, so it establishes integration consistency rather than independent bit-exact arithmetic. Guest flush/sign and OMOD gating have literal witnesses, and seven cases per precision inherited from rocjitsu division_test.cpp at ffc144c564c independently anchor fused scaling direction, subnormal midpoint, avoided overflow and cancellation. All CPU selectors, sequenced mt19937 draws, masks and overlapping split destinations are covered. Active RDNA3 OMOD remains loose-only; unavailable exact optional state (including output-flush cases) is rejected atomically. Raw equality in the differential test is intentional; mathematical loose arithmetic tolerances are a separate family concern.
diagnostics: Integration checks identify architecture/width/precision/guest/mode/CPU. Borrowed literal witnesses identify precision/lane and preserve exact expected bit patterns; no hardware equivalence is inferred merely from the differential oracle.

scope: FP32/64 DIV_SCALE across RDNA3/RDNA4 and both widths. gfx1201 hardware digests independently anchor 576 B/C pairs, both legal A roles after NEG, and 64 modifier variants, including per-lane condition bits. Broader seeded mt19937, CPU/host-mode and alias loops are differential against baseline exact GoC and establish integration consistency, not numerical equivalence independently. Both semantics, all available CPU selectors, masks, split and unaligned scalar-output aliases, guards and error precedence are covered. Active RDNA3 OMOD is explicitly loose-only. Exact raw results/conditions are appropriate for these borrowed-model and differential checks; no approximate division quotient is computed here.
diagnostics: Hardware digests localize to precision/CPU/role-modifier column (576 inputs); separate literals explain guest and NaN branches. Differential per-lane and whole-storage checks localize integration failures. Native Wave64 hardware capture is not claimed.

scope: FP32/64 RDNA4 DIV_FMAS in both wave widths. Exception corpora now verify preservation of every pre-existing bit outside the seven captured flag bits, not only the highest bit. Ordinary FMA invalid-operation assumptions do not apply: DIV_FMAS suppresses invalid and input-denormal flags, whose evidence here remains the capture digests. Loose reporting is skipped; invalid calls preserve state. Architecture/guest restrictions are reviewed separately.
